extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It combines 6,141 examples from existing multimodal datasets and three newly created datasets covering tasks such as figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problems, textbook question answering, and visual question answering.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We collected nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings, including four for GPS, two for MWP with visual contexts of synthetic scenes, abstract diagrams, and tables, and two for TQA on college curricula. We also reviewed more than 70 VQA datasets, collecting 19 publicly available datasets with math-related instances, using heuristic rules to automatically select candidate examples and then having three expert annotators manually label them. In addition, we introduced three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA) sourced from puzzle test figures, functional plots, and academic illustrations/papers, with manual annotation and review.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some false positive examples remained after automatic filtration; these were then manually labeled by three expert annotators and resolved by majority voting.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MathQA datasets in multimodal settings; publicly available VQA datasets with math-related instances; puzzle test figures on online learning platforms; functional plots; academic illustrations, tables, figures, and charts from online education resources; papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Expert annotators labeled whether each problem involved mathematical reasoning using an annotation tool. Annotators were trained with detailed instructions and examples, and they used three labels: Yes, No, and Unsure. They could also leave comments if they found anything incorrect or offensive.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: An annotation tool with a GUI was developed for labeling.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was measured with Fleiss Kappa among three annotators, yielding a score of 0.775, indicating substantial agreement.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may have coverage gaps in certain types of mathematical problems and visuals, and its annotations come from heterogeneous sources with non-unified formats and structures.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage is incomplete for some problem/visual types; scalability and generalizability to other domains are a concern; only 85.6% of examples have annotations; annotations are heterogeneous and lack a unified format; the benchmark focused only on the most recent and prominent models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve understanding and enhancement of AI capabilities in mathematical and visual reasoning, with ongoing maintenance to refine data noise and evolve the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking/evaluating model performance on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts; future iterations aim to broaden problem and visual coverage and provide unified annotations. The benchmark is for ongoing evaluation rather than a fixed one-time release.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process; the maintainers commit to refining potential data noise, maintaining the datasets, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To ensure that each source dataset is well represented in testmini and to maintain a distribution in testmini closely resembling the whole set, we adopted this sampling strategy: (1) first, randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) then, randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on their proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For non-math-targeted VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates; examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words were selected. These examples were then manually labeled by expert annotators, using majority voting to finalize the collection. The dataset also underwent quality checks.
